# Rear Headrest Removal on the 2010 Ford Fusion

Attempting to service or replace the rear headrests on a 2010 Ford Fusion reveals a specific mechanical constraint that often confuses DIYers. The primary limitation is found in the adjustment mechanism located within the driver-side rail. This rail contains an actuation button designed to allow the headrest to slide forward and backward for height adjustment. However, this mechanism is not a universal release key; pushing the button on the driver side will only lower the headrest to its minimum safe position or retract it slightly, but it does not disengage the locking pin required to remove the unit entirely.

To successfully extract the rear headrests, you must bypass the standard adjustment logic. The physical removal process requires direct access to the mounting hardware concealed within the seatback structure. Before beginning, ensure the vehicle is parked on a level surface and the ignition is off. You will need a set of trim removal tools to pry open the plastic covers without causing damage, along with a socket set or screwdriver depending on the specific sub-assembly configuration of your interior panel.

The procedure involves carefully prying away the lower portion of the seatback fabric or plastic trim where the headrest post enters the seat frame. On the 2010 Fusion, this often requires leveraging a flat tool behind the base of the headrest post to expose the retaining screw or clip. Once the cover is removed, you will see the threaded rod that connects the headrest to the mounting bracket inside the seatback.

If your vehicle utilizes a threaded locking mechanism (which is common in this model year), you must rotate the headrest post counter-clockwise using the adjustment button while simultaneously applying upward pressure on the headrest itself. This action unscrews the post from the internal bracket. It is critical to note that the driver-side rail button serves only as an actuator for the screw mechanism; it does not mechanically decouple the post from the seatback. You must manually rotate the post until it is fully disengaged before you can lift the headrest assembly out of the seat cavity.

Once the threaded connection is broken, remove any remaining retaining clips or screws that secure the bracket to the seatback foam or frame. With these fasteners removed, the rear headrests should slide freely out of the seatback opening. Be prepared for some resistance if the mechanism has been used extensively, as friction can build up over time. Apply steady, even pressure rather than jerking motions to avoid snapping plastic clips or damaging the upholstery stitching.

If you are replacing these components with aftermarket units, verify that the new headrests match the specific mounting style of the 2010 Fusion. Some universal kits require drilling new holes in the seatback, which can compromise structural integrity and void warranties. Stick to OEM-spec replacements when possible to maintain the original safety ratings and fitment tolerances.
